Definition: A proper name, including alternative, shortened or foreign forms of the same name.
Example: Jove and Jupiter for one god; Boreas and Aquilo for one wind.
Venus' son (Cupid); Bright Pleiad's child (Mercury, son of Maia).

Definition: Names someone by a more distant ancestor, or by a sibling.
Example: Atlas' grandson (Mercury); Phoronis (Io, sister of Phoroneus).

Definition: Names someone by their standing to another person in the scene, and so only works inside it.
A title under which the god was actually worshipped.
Example: the Thunderer (Jupiter, Latin Tonans); Paean (Apollo as healer).

Definition: Names a god by a place sacred to them — a birthplace, a shrine, an oracle.
Example: the Delian lord (Apollo, born on Delos); Cyllenius (Mercury).

Definition: Names someone by what they do or what they govern.
Example: the archer-god (Apollo); the king of gods (Jupiter).

Definition: Names someone by a physical trait, a possession, or a stock adjective.
A whole descriptive phrase standing in place of a name.
Example: that Arcadian king (Lycaön); worshiped by a linened throng (Io, as Isis).

Definition: A name used for the thing it governs, or a thing used for the person.
Example: Ceres' seeds for grain; Nereus for the sea; Love for Cupid.

Definition: A bare common noun, with the context left to supply the referent.
Example: the goddess (Themis, later Juno); the nymph (Daphne, later Io).
